source.title: Accelerating GPU Inference of Large Language Models with Moderately Unstructured Sparse Weight Matrices
source.summary: With the growing deployment of large language models (LLMs), LLM inference cost has become a key challenge. Pruning techniques that introduce sparsity into weight matrices can accelerate inference. However, maintaining model quality typically limits pruning to moderate unstructured sparsity (around 50\%). At these sparsity levels, none of the existing GPU kernels for sparse matrix multiplication (SpMM) can outperform their dense counterparts. This paper proposes an efficient GPU inference method for LLMs with moderate sparsity. We propose a three-layer matrix storage format comprising: (i) a Sparse-TC layer enabling sparse tensor cores to accelerate SpMM; (ii) a Slot-Filling layer using parallel differential distance for matrix compression while supporting low-cost on-chip decoding; (iii) a lightweight Residual Layer ensuring correct SpMM computation. Building on this format, we design a SpMM kernel that jointly utilizes sparse tensor cores and CUDA cores. This design enables an efficient execution pipeline and overlaps on-chip computation with memory access. Evaluations show that our work is the first to outperform dense matrix multiplication on modern GPUs equipped with high-bandwidth memory (HBM). It achieves up to 1.64x kernel-level speedup over SpInfer (EuroSys'25, Best paper) and up to 1.41x end-to-end speedups over FlashLLM (VLDB'24). Our source code: https://github.com/moui0/cudac.

previous_facts.title: Accelerating GPU Inference of Large Language Models with Moderately Unstructured Sparse Weight Matrices
previous_facts.event_hint: DAC 2026 paper proposing sparse matrix inference acceleration for LLMs on GPUs
previous_facts.problem: At moderate unstructured sparsity (~50%), existing GPU kernels for sparse matrix multiplication (SpMM) cannot outperform dense counterparts, limiting inference acceleration while maintaining model quality.
previous_facts.mechanism: Three-layer matrix storage format: (i) Sparse-TC layer enabling sparse tensor cores to accelerate SpMM; (ii) Slot-Filling layer using parallel differential distance (PDD) encoding for matrix compression with low-cost on-chip decoding; (iii) lightweight Residual Layer (CSR format) for remaining non-zeros. Co-optimized SpMM kernel jointly utilizes sparse tensor cores and CUDA cores with pipelined execution overlapping computation with memory access.

evidence.claim: Kernel achieves up to 1.64× speedup over SpInfer at 50% sparsity
Kernel achieves up to 1.81× speedup over FlashLLM at 50% sparsity
End-to-end inference throughput up to 41.4% higher than FlashLLM for OPT-30B
Peak memory usage reduced by 21.4% compared to dense baseline
Format conversion cost is one-time: 41.1s for OPT-30B, 92.6s for OPT-66B

previous_facts.evaluation_context: NVIDIA H100 SXM5 GPUs with 80GB HBM3, NVLink interconnect; OPT-30B and OPT-66B models pruned with Wanda algorithm; batch sizes 8/16/32; sparsity levels 50%/60%/70%; input/output sequence length 512; GCC 12.3.0 and NVCC 12.6.
previous_facts.limitations: Does not outperform FlashLLM under high sparsity due to zero-padding requirements; constrained during compute-bound prefill phase with large N (runs slower than cuBLAS); targets decoding phase optimization; requires GPUs with sparse tensor cores and HBM; incurs slightly higher memory usage than SpInfer due to bitmap encoding in baseline method. Absolute throughput in tokens/second or latency in milliseconds not reported. HBM bandwidth utilization or memory traffic measurements not provided. Power consumption or performance-per-watt not measured. Supplement contains only acknowledgments and references—no additional experimental data addressing evidence gaps.
previous_facts.project_relevance: Addresses GPU memory bandwidth bottleneck in LLM inference through sparse matrix computation co-design with modern GPU hardware (sparse tensor cores + HBM). Relevant to direction on AI accelerator memory interface and hardware-software co-design. Demonstrates 1.64× kernel speedup and 21.4% memory reduction at 50% sparsity on H100, showing how algorithm-hardware specialization can extract performance from memory-bound workloads. However, absolute throughput numbers (tokens/second), HBM bandwidth utilization measurements, and power efficiency metrics are not reported—key evidence gaps for assessing real-world deployment value.
